quests.title: The Hat and the Warden
quests.summary: The Wardens want the old man's hat and staff. Give them up and earn the High Warden's trust, or keep them and keep his voice close.

stages.description: A Warden lieutenant has ridden into Millbrook asking for you by name.

objectives.description: Meet Lieutenant Hale at the Mill Wheel

stages.description: Lieutenant Hale wants the old man's hat and staff before dusk.

objectives.description: Hand the hat and staff to Hale
Or hide them under the old mill's floorboards
Or refuse him to his face

stages.description: Hale's escort has drawn steel. Nobody in Millbrook has seen a Warden fight before.
It's done, one way or another. Tam saw everything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A Warden in a pressed blue coat sits at the best table in the Mill Wheel, with two armed riders behind him. He does not get up.
You'll be the farm kid with the sparks. Lieutenant Hale, Wardens of the Crown. Sit.
Sergeant Brask's report says you kept a hat and a staff belonging to the man on the hill. Honest of you. The High Warden wants them.
Funny thing. A shepherd says a farm kid walked down off that hill carrying a staff. Sergeant Brask's report says the old man left nothing at all. Someone's wrong.
The hat and the staff are evidence in a matter of the Crown. The High Warden wants them. Bring them to me before dusk.

choices.text: Why does the High Warden care about one old man?

lines.text: That's above both of us, farm kid. High Warden Varrow doesn't explain herself to lieutenants, and she certainly doesn't explain herself to you.
A vagrant. A danger. Someone who should have stayed in whatever hole he crawled out of. That's all you need to know.
Before dusk. Don't make me come looking.
Well? The hat and the staff.

choices.text: I don't have them. Search me if you like.
They're not yours. You're not getting them.
Not yet. I need more time.

lines.text: Sensible. The High Warden remembers sensible people. If you ever need the Wardens, ask for me by name.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: As the staff leaves your hand it stops humming, as if it had been holding its breath. You feel oddly cold.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Hale's riders turn out your pockets, your pack and the barn. They find a great deal of hay and nothing else.
...Fine. But I'll be watching you, farm kid. So will she.
Wrong answer.
The sun won't wait, and neither will I.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A loose board in the old mill's loft. Tam showed you this hiding place years ago. Nobody else knows it.

choices.text: Hide the hat and staff under the floorboards.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The staff hums once as the board settles over it, like a sigh of relief.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You leave the board as it is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tam has been waiting by the gate.
You just gave them away? He gave those to YOU. Not to the Wardens. You.

choices.text: It was the right thing to do. They're the law.
It was the safe thing to do. For you, and for Ma.

lines.text: You lied to a Warden. To his face. While they turned out the barn. ...That's the best thing I've ever seen.

choices.text: Nobody can know where they are, Tam. Not even Ma.
Don't get any ideas. Lying to Wardens is not a game.

lines.text: Everyone saw. The whole village saw you fight the Wardens. Ma's going to... I don't even know what Ma's going to do.
Do you think he's really gone? The old man?

choices.text: No. I think he's somewhere. I think he's waiting.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tam nods, very seriously, and doesn't let go of your sleeve for a long time.
Move along, farm kid.
